title: Star-Pack Dominance and Forced-Prime CRT Lower Bounds for the Agoh–Giuga Conjecture
scope: Exhausts the normal-set bound for the Agoh-Giuga conjecture (8,135 factors / 321,053 max prime / 40,733 digits; 352,757 exact outside Leaf 2) via a 4-line Star-Pack Reciprocal Dominance Lemma and 7-leaf partition, then breaks past the normal-set ceiling via mod-16 congruences, elementary a >= 2 splitting, forced-prime CRT, and 846 exact 2D lattice witnesses to prove unconditionally omega(n) >= 8,138, P(n) >= 326,057, and >= 40,922 decimal digits, plus sharp dichotomies and an r = 2 giant-prime structural barrier.
gate_basis: src/verify_agoh_giuga_certificate.py independently re-verifies all 7 Star-Pack leaves, exhaustive mod-16 table, elementary a >= 2 bounds, all 846 exact (U, R) lattice witnesses, and zero-float Lagrangian star inequalities in ~15 seconds using Python 3 stdlib only (AST-audited zero floats). tests/test_agoh_giuga_tier2.py runs 11 unit, AST zero-float, DP2 soundness, r=2 boundary, and fail-closed tamper tests.
dependencies: Python 3 standard library only (zero external packages, zero floating-point arithmetic in the verifier); TeX Live / latexmk only for optional PDF rebuild.
limitations: Terminal status: partial theorem. The full Agoh-Giuga conjecture remains open; Theorem 5.1 proves a sharp structural barrier explaining why local CRT + 2D lattice refutation leaves 3 <= N_0 <= ~10^17704 open for two-giant-prime completions.
Not externally peer reviewed; no interactive proof assistant (Lean, Coq, Isabelle) was used.
Novelty wording is bounded to literature indexed through October 2026 (citing Mavrotheris Aug 2026 Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22085830 for the mod-8 congruence and Lopez Oct 2026 arXiv:2610.09129v2).
External literature PDFs are cited, not reproduced.
